summary: Comments on RFC 580. The author supports requiring machine-readable protocol documents but objects to preferring NLS files, since many sites have no way to convert their own text into NLS.

eli5.summary: He agrees protocols should be sent as computer files but not that they must be in one special program's format, since not everyone can use it.

subtitle: A short objection to requiring protocol documents to be written as NLS files.

tldr.problem: RFC 580 asked for machine-readable protocol documents, preferably as NLS files, but most sites had no way to convert their own text into NLS.
tldr.mechanism: The author backs machine-readable documents but objects to the phrase "preferably as nls files", and asks for a general program that converts nicely formatted text to NLS files.
tldr.outcome: The note is a comment only. It suggests the journal mail-receiving program might serve as the converter, if it were better documented and publicised.

sections.title: Support With One Objection
sections.content:
R. Clements of BBN-TENEX writes in reply to RFC 580. He fully supports the requirement for machine-readable protocol documents, noting that in his situation the line-printer is a much more reliable device than the copying machine.

His objection is to a single phrase in RFC 580: "preferably as nls files". He is clear that the problem is the lack of conversion mechanisms into NLS, not the retrieval process or NLS itself.
sections.eli5: He likes the idea of sharing documents as computer files. He just does not like being told to use one special program that few people can feed.

sections.title: Why Sites Cannot Easily Use NLS
sections.content: Most sites have their own text editors and RUNOFF programs (or equivalents). Most large protocol documents are prepared at least partly by secretarial help, and those people should be able to work on the home machine in languages they already know.
sections.eli5: People write in the tools they know. Making them learn another tool just for sharing is a big ask.

sections.title: The Requested Converter
sections.content:
The author wants a general program for converting nicely formatted text to NLS files. It should preferably be clever, but at the least generally available and predictable.

He suggests that the program which receives mail for the journal might do the job. If so, it needs documentation beyond the mail-oriented RFC 543, and its existence and usage need to be publicised.
sections.eli5: He asks for a helper machine that turns ordinary writing into the special format, and for someone to tell everyone it exists.

references.text: RFC 580, the document being commented on.
RFC 543, the mail-oriented document that describes the journal mail program.
